## Concepts introduced

::: {.chips}
<span class="chip">the Ch 1–7 chain as a single argument</span><span class="chip">where an error does the most damage</span>
:::

## Tuesday — The chain, argued backwards

::: {.case}
Tuesday is not a lecture. You work the problems you got wrong and reconstruct the causal chain from Chapter 1 to Chapter 7 on the board, in both directions.

::: {.qn}
Success is contested, so strategy decides what to select, so structure decides who can deliver it, so scope decides what <em>it</em> is, so estimates price it, so the network sequences it, so risk says how wrong all of that might be. Where in that chain does an error do the most damage, and why there?
:::
:::

## Tuesday — integration

Not a lecture. Work the problems you got wrong and reconstruct the chain from Chapter 1 to
Chapter 7 on the board, in both directions. Bring your marked-up studio work.

## Thursday — midterm examination

::: {.studio}
#### 75 minutes · closed book · closed notes · no computers or phones

A non-programmable calculator is permitted and recommended. Covers **Larson Chapters 1–7**.

**AI use: Level 1 — prohibited.** No AI during the examination, and none during a conceptual assignment while it is open. See the [policy](../syllabus.qmd#use-of-generative-artificial-intelligence). Using AI to *prepare* is encouraged — that is what the retrieval prompt is for.
Earned value is Week 11 and is **not** on this paper.

| Part | Weight | What it asks |
|:--|--:|:--|
| A · Short concept | 30% | Definitions, distinctions, and *why* a distinction matters |
| B · Quantitative | 45% | A network with a full float table, a crash step, a three-point estimate. Arithmetic is checkable — method earns the marks |
| C · Judgement | 25% | A short scenario. Choose, and defend against the strongest alternative |

: {tbl-colwidths="[26,12,62]"}

**How to prepare.** Re-work the studio problems without the key, then check. Use the retrieval
prompt in [AI Studio](../ai.qmd) for mixed questions across all seven weeks — mixing is what makes
retrieval practice work, and it is the one form of AI use that helps on a closed-book exam.

**What is not tested.** Memorized process catalogues, ITTO tables, or edition numbers. If you would
look it up in thirty seconds on the job, it is not on the paper.
:::
